design_evidence_scope.baseline: Source inspection finds the current room renders count-derived strands and one phase glyph between two circles. The operator reports that its motion does not explain the selected AI task or governed crossing.
design_evidence_scope.comparison: Same actual provider route, changed receiver-facing presentation. Source review and declared geometry do not establish human comprehension.
design_evidence_scope.millipoint_basis: Baseline and candidate carry identical neutral structural values; no measured improvement or invented audience score.
design_evidence_scope.gate_limit: PASS verifies the declared consequence route and invariants. Candidate browser witnesses and actual event-to-pixel checks remain required.

evidence_basis: The operator requests an expressive, almost cartoon-like live room explaining selected project and real AIA transport.
Current source exposes selected document IDs, withheld count, local binding admission, client submission, response arrival, admitted result and structured reported missingness.
Provider-internal attention, reasoning progress and hidden-state exposure are not supplied by these events.
transformations: Replace the abstract two-circle route with three persistent places: local pocket, rule gate, AI desk.
Attach cards and source references to the actual selected project; keep private material in the local pocket throughout.
Drive glyph relations and visible movement only from the same admitted event snapshot.
Retain submission and response history when the request stops or the return is held.

visible_condition.plain_language: Watch your chosen work travel with its rules. The papers you keep here stay in your pocket; a returned answer comes back for checking.
visible_condition.now: Choose a project. See which papers can travel and which stay here.
visible_condition.why: Give the AI useful context while keeping the unselected layer out of this request.
visible_condition.exact: Inspect the same event, selected source IDs, binding result, response references and hold reason behind each motion.

available_affordances.purpose: Send the explicitly selected fictional project documents to the configured server-side Gemini route, then validate the returned candidate before presenting it as usable output.
available_affordances.irreversible_consequence: Selected documents are transmitted to the configured Gemini provider after the send gesture; leaving the workspace cannot recall that transmission.

route_topology.entry: Project and prompt workspace with visible selected-document scope
route_topology.exit: Rest or leave at any step; completed provider transmission remains recorded
missing_inputs: Candidate three-engine visual witnesses and human comprehension remain separate observations.

steps.label: See the useful task and exactly which documents can travel
Choose a project or add your own supported document
Send selected documents to Gemini with one explicit gesture
See request progress and the actual model result
See what passed or why the returned result was held
Inspect the receipt, open the project in Marrowline, or export its portable governance
Stop new work or leave with the event history intact

causal_structure.input: One selected fictional or operator-supplied AI project, classified documents and explicit request gesture
causal_structure.operator: local document selection -> server-side provider request -> structured model candidate -> deterministic return validation -> useful result or HOLD
causal_structure.observable: Persistent source pocket, governed crossing and receiver desk change on local selection, actual binding result, submission, observed return and deterministic admission. Pending motion shows waiting only.
causal_structure.authority: The send gesture authorizes the displayed provider transmission. Model prose never authorizes local-only document release or downstream execution.
equations: observed request timing != provider hidden-state measurement

research_frame.question: Can the same real request route explain what stays local, what has been submitted, and what may be presented after return through one persistent living-room composition?
research_frame.hypothesis: Stable places, task-specific paper props, verb-first phase captions and event-caused crossings make the route inspectable before technical terminology. Human comprehension remains unmeasured.
observable_behavior: Changing the selected demo changes room task and source state without network activity.
Unselected documents remain on the local shelf in every request phase.
Binding success appears only after authorization succeeds.
Pending never claims delivery, provider reading or reasoning percentage.
A returned candidate remains under checking until admitted.
A stopped request retains any already-observed submission or response history.
Reduced motion retains all route facts; rest stops render cadence without changing authority.
Replay traverses recorded events on the same animation owner without creating a provider request or authority mutation.
Editing task, rules or source selection refreshes the prepared projection and invalidates stale runnable output.
falsifier: A private paper crosses the gate or appears on the receiver desk.
An animated progress loop creates an apparent additional request or delivery event.
A binding badge appears before local authorization succeeds.
A held response becomes an accepted answer, release gesture or completed-work glow.
Stopping after submission restores the visual claim that nothing left.
Source-reference or missingness marks appear before a returned structured report supplies them.
Changing plain/auditor view changes selected scope, binding or admitted operations.
Motion pauses only by discarding evidence or hiding the current route.
The rendered room represents a different demo than the task actually sent.
The renderer opens its own perpetual animation clock.
Replay submits a new request, admits a historical candidate as current, or overwrites live request state.
The room continues to show a previous project after the operator edits its task or scope.
abstention_conditions: Provider or network failure remains a held request with exact available history.
Without a governed event, decorative motion must not claim a transport event.
alternative_explanations: Clearer animation may aid demonstration without establishing children or first-time visitors understand the workflow.
A successful bounded model response does not establish every remote receiver enforces exported governance.
expected_failure_modes: Cute paper props obscure the actual chosen document counts.
Timer progress impersonates hidden provider work.
Held state erases previous actual crossing.
Private text leaks into SVG labels or new visual receipts.

missingness: Candidate three-engine visual witnesses and human comprehension remain separate observations.

allowed_claims: The room projects locally observed request events and explicitly reported response fields.
The same selected task and origin rules determine both plain and auditor views.
Reduced-motion and rest views preserve the route facts.
forbidden_claims: A design gate PASS proves human comprehension or provider-internal visibility.
A waiting loop measures provider thinking, latent reconstruction or external-origin information.
A submitted request has been recalled by stopping its animation.
Reported source references prove provider internal use.

transfer_context.shared_relation_candidate: Persistent places and monotonic event history can teach a governed crossing without implying provider-internal observability.
observable_correspondence: At least three project selections must share the same invariant route while displaying their actual selected scope.
alternative_explanations: A successful model answer may result from this bounded task and says nothing about unavailable host enforcement.
